audit.why: TF owns levels 1-5 (Veigar slow, immobile, stack-starved), Veigar flips at 6 with cage-R and out-scales late. Page prose and 51.6% WR over 1909 games agree; only the full-layer chart lagged.
Spikes complete and grounded: TF 3-5 dominance, Veigar 6 flip, first AP item + stacks, infinite late scaling. All four content spikes present.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit despite Event Horizon's 20s rank-1 cooldown being the matchup's whole rhythm; his R is 120/90/60 and point-and-click (no dodge).
audit.why: Kit: E cd 20/18.5/17/15.5/14, 725 range, edge-stun cage; R cd 120/90/60, 650 range, targeted execute; Q 1000-range line skillshot blocked by the first two units.
audit.corrected: Added the numbers. Edge-only stun mechanic already correctly stated. Gold card is point-and-click so his no-mobility kit cannot dodge it — now stated in the chart whys.
Replaced with Veigar-grounded bodies matching their titles.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W gold card has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — 20s cooldown at rank 1, 14s at max; only the cage EDGE stuns — hold near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. His R is 120/90/60s. - Your W gold card has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it goes right.

edits.before: Lock gold off-screen, walk up once, card-auto-Q, and leave — one stun-chunk per cycle is all the lane asks of you.
edits.after: Wild Cards farm outside his 1000-range Baleful Strike — throw Q only at carded or distant targets and step straight back.

edits.before: Cycling cards inside his engage range for stacked-deck greed — TF dies in exactly one mistimed auto-walk per game; don't pre-book it.
edits.after: From level 6 his cage-into-R combo one-shots with any stacks — a blind shove into 725-range Event Horizon is a scripted death.

edits.before: Q-farm from range and concede the duel question entirely — your level 1 is a wallet, not a weapon.
edits.after: Veigar level 1 is slow and immobile — Blue Card poke and a hard shove out-pressure him from the start.

edits.before: W online: the gold card re-prices his every step-up. Lock yellow when he walks forward and the lane behaves.
edits.after: W online: Wild Cards clear while he stacks — his no-mobility kit cannot dodge a gold card walk-up; tempo is yours.

edits.before: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus card cycling is a real short trade — but your game is the clock, not the lane.
edits.after: Full kit: stacked-deck autos plus a gold card he cannot dodge — his 20s Event Horizon is the only trade he has.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q the wave, lock cards on cooldown, and watch side lanes like they're your KDA.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — keep shoving and roaming freely while his stacks are tiny and his cage sits on 20s.

edits.before: At 5 you retain lane control before his cage-R combo comes fully online.
edits.after: At 6 Destiny's map pressure outweighs a cage-R combo you can stand back from.
